items.title: Joseph Ralph Robinson Interview, 1960-10-12
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...old Jim Humphrey didn't like that? ... [INTERVIEWEE] And I appreciated it. I didn't like it...

ctx.x: He said, well, that's good. I said, first and last, I guess I'll catch you on Jack Carey and them. You know, one musician, they used to back... They wag your tail together, you know, and play. I said, next time, but Rousin and Mark, remember what I'm telling you. If I catch you on the bed where, uh, with Jack Carey, they're playing out in the street like that. Don't come to me, no. I said, no, I don't go to them. You didn't like that kind of music, huh?
No, I didn't. I did not. I mean, he didn't, uh, old Jim Humphrey didn't like that? He didn't like that either. Oh, no, he didn't like that. He didn't, huh? No, he didn't.

And I appreciated it. I didn't like it, but I said, playing out, you know, in the street. Yeah. And so we used to have a little band. We used to rehearse at a place they called, uh, right here in this city. And, uh, place they called, uh, it's a church. They got a school there, I think. Right downtown there on Tulane Avenue, I think. We were in that vicinity. And, uh, we used to play, and the boys all, you know, they used to come in the back of me, I was playing, uh, the first client. Is that near, yeah. Is that…
